title: Targum on Genesis
credit: J. W. Etheridge, 1862–1865, is public domain. The Google-scan PDF in update_01 is an image of that edition and has no extractable text, so this desk ships original notes, not a page dump.

sections.title: What a Targum is
paragraphs: A Targum is an Aramaic rendering of the Hebrew Scriptures, read beside the Hebrew in the synagogue. Onkelos on the Torah is the most careful. Jonathan ben Uzziel is a wider paraphrase on the Prophets. Etheridge put both into Victorian English. That English is public domain.

sections.title: Genesis 1 beside Onkelos
paragraphs: Genesis 1:1 in the King James is “In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.” Onkelos stays close: in the beginning the Lord created the heavens and the earth. Jonathan’s wider paraphrase adds “with wisdom.” This desk keeps the King James in the Bible window and this note in Extra-canon.

sections.title: How to read it here
paragraphs: Open Genesis in the Bible. Extra-canon on the verse bar will search this shelf when the word is long enough. Etheridge’s printed pages remain in the PDF; they are not copied into the bundle because the scan has no text layer.
